title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 10th District
area: Parts of Essex, Hudson, and Union counties, including most of Newark, East Orange, Irvington, Elizabeth, and Jersey City.

context.text: LaMonica McIver won the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026, defeating Lawrence Poster. Carmen Bucco won the Republican primary unopposed. Both advance to the November 3, 2026 general election, which is uncontested by any third-party or independent candidates.

summary.text: LaMonica McIver is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District, first elected in a September 2024 special election to succeed the late Rep. Donald Payne Jr., and re-elected to a full term in November 2024. She previously served on the Newark City Council from 2018 to 2024, including as Council President. She sits on the House Committees on Homeland Security and Small Business. In May 2025, federal prosecutors charged her with assault stemming from a visit to a Newark ICE detention facility.

background.text: Born in Newark, New Jersey, in 1986.
Earned a bachelor's degree in English literature from Bloomfield College in 2008 and a graduate degree in education leadership, management and policy from Seton Hall University in 2011.
Worked as an administrator, including as Executive Director for the Essex Regional Educational Services Commission, before entering elected office full time.
Founded Newark G.A.L.S., Inc. in 2012, an organization focused on developing female leaders.
Elected to the Newark City Council (Central Ward) in 2018 as the youngest woman ever to serve on the council, and served as Council President from 2022 to 2024.
Elected to the U.S. House in a September 2024 special election to complete the term of the late Rep. Donald M. Payne Jr., becoming the first Black woman to represent NJ-10.

priorities.text: Addressing the interconnected challenges of affordability, housing, healthcare and education costs, and the local impact of climate change, including flooding in the district.
Securing safe, affordable housing, including policies to increase affordable housing options, protect tenants' rights, and address housing discrimination.
Combatting food insecurity through stronger nutrition assistance programs and access to nutritious food.
Gun violence prevention measures including universal background checks, closing background-check loopholes, and waiting periods.

positions.summary: Supports stricter gun laws, including universal background checks, closing loopholes in the background-check system, and waiting periods, calling gun violence a public health crisis.
Says she will always stand for protecting a woman's right to choose.
positions.quote: I will always stand for protecting a woman’s right to choose, for every American to have access to the ballot box, and to live without fear of violence.

positions.summary: Supports policies to increase affordable housing options, protect tenants' rights, and address housing discrimination.

Publicly opposed the reopening of the Delaney Hall ICE detention facility in Newark and characterized her related federal assault charge as an effort to criminalize legislative oversight of the facility.
positions.quote: We were fulfilling our lawful oversight responsibilities, as members of Congress have done many times before, and our visit should have been peaceful and short. Instead, ICE agents created an unnecessary and unsafe confrontation when they chose to arrest Mayor Baraka. The charges against me are purely political—they mischaracterize and distort my actions, and are meant to criminalize and deter legislative oversight.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Subcommittees on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure, and Transportation and Maritime Security) and the House Committee on Small Business (Subcommittees on Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access; Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; and Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations) in the 119th Congress.

On May 19, 2025, the interim U.S. Attorney for the District of New Jersey announced federal assault charges against McIver under 18 U.S.C. § 111(a)(1), stemming from a May 9, 2025 visit by McIver and other officials to the Delaney Hall ICE detention facility in Newark, during which Newark Mayor Ras Baraka was arrested (charges against Baraka were later dropped).

candidates.name: Carmen Bucco
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Carmen Bucco is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District. He owns Bucco Couture, a tailoring business, and previously ran unsuccessfully for this seat in 2024 and for NJ State Senate District 20 in 2023.

background.text: Born in New Jersey and graduated from Nutley High School in 1990.
Owner of Bucco Couture, a tailoring business; describes growing up in the foster care system.
Unsuccessful Republican candidate for NJ-10 in 2024 and for New Jersey State Senate District 20 in 2023.

priorities.text: Supporting law enforcement and first responders, and opposing policies he describes as "tying the hands of law enforcement."
priorities.quote: Tying the hands of law enforcement only endangers our way of life. We must always support our police and first responders and need to be tough on violent crimes while focusing on keeping our communities safe.

priorities.text: Reducing taxes and government spending, saying current policies are "driving inflation and impeding our quality of life."
priorities.quote: The policies of today are driving inflation and impeding our quality of life. We need to control our spending at the state level and stop frivolous spending.

priorities.text: Supporting small businesses by reducing regulatory burdens and expanding access to funding.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a supporter of the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms and says it should never be infringed upon.
positions.quote: I am a supporter of the Second Amendment -- the right to keep and bear arms to protect ourselves and this constitutional right should never be infringed upon.

positions.summary: Says communities must "always support our police and first responders" and be tough on violent crime.
Says taxes are "out of control" and calls for controlling government spending rather than raising taxes.

researchNotes: Ballot-access and candidate-slate facts drawn from Ballotpedia; not independently cross-checked against the NJ Division of Elections. Congress.gov and govtrack.us were unreachable in this environment, so a full list of bills McIver has sponsored in the 119th Congress could not be independently verified; per research guidance, her federal floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script. The current status (trial date, plea, or resolution) of McIver's May 2025 federal assault charge could not be confirmed as of this research date. Carmen Bucco has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his 2026-specific positions could not be found beyond his general campaign-site issues page (some content dates to a prior 2024 State Senate run) and his research depth is marked basic.
